boards.name: Town Square
boards.tagline: The notice board by the lifts. News, notices, and neighbourly chatter.

boards.name: Séance Circle
boards.tagline: Ask for help, offer a hand. One neighbour at a time.

boards.name: The Library
boards.tagline: Books, films, and songs worth your evening.

boards.name: Workshop
boards.tagline: Trade skills, tools, and know-how. No money changes hands unless you say so.

boards.name: Lost & Found
boards.tagline: Lost something? Found something? Pin it here.

posts.author: Mara, Flat 12
posts.body: The lift stopped between the third and fourth floors this morning, so it is stairs for everyone until the engineer comes on Thursday. If you have heavy bags, knock on Flat 2 and Dennis will help carry them up. The stairs are fine, just slow, so please leave a little extra time.

replies.author: Dennis, Flat 2
replies.body: Happy to help with bags, and I have a spare trolley in the bike room if anyone needs it.

posts.title: The lift is out of order again

posts.author: Dennis, Flat 2
posts.body: The parcel shelf by the front door is full again, and three boxes have been there since last week. If your name is on one, please collect it before Friday so the courier has somewhere to put the new ones. Anything unclaimed after Friday goes to the caretaker's office.
posts.title: Parcel room: please collect your boxes

posts.author: Ines, Flat 31
posts.body: The rooftop beds still need watering twice a week, even in November, and the rota has two empty slots. It takes ten minutes and the key is on the hook by the lift. If you would like a slot, put your name and flat number here and I will add you to the list.

replies.author: Priya, Flat 26
replies.body: I will take Thursdays. The rosemary up there is doing better than mine ever did.

posts.title: Rooftop garden watering rota for November

posts.author: Alan, Flat 7
posts.body: This is just a friendly note that quiet hours in the building start at ten in the evening. The walls are thinner than they look, especially between the kitchens on the second floor. Nobody is in trouble, and nobody has complained — let us keep it that way.
posts.title: Quiet hours start at ten — a gentle reminder

posts.author: Rosa, Flat 19
posts.body: We are holding a short building meeting on Tuesday at seven in the laundry room, mostly about the lift contract and the bike room. It should take half an hour and there will be tea. If you cannot come, leave a note here and I will bring your point to the table.

replies.author: Jonas, Flat 41
replies.body: I cannot make Tuesday, but please ask about a second rail in the bike room. There are not enough hooks.

posts.title: Building meeting, Tuesday 7pm in the laundry room

posts.author: Priya, Flat 26
posts.body: Someone left a paper bag of lemons by the lifts this morning with a note saying help yourself. I took two and they made the best tea I have had all week. If that was you, thank you — and the tree they came from must be very loved.

replies.author: Ines, Flat 31
replies.body: That was me, from my sister's tree. There will be more next week if the frost holds off.

posts.title: Thank you, whoever left the lemons by the lifts

posts.author: Tom, Flat 8
posts.body: I need to put up two shelves in the kitchen, and buying a drill for one job feels wasteful. If someone has one I could borrow on Saturday, I will return it the same evening, clean and charged. I can offer a home-cooked supper in return.

replies.author: Marcus, Flat 33
replies.body: Borrow mine, Tom. Flat 33, knock any time after five.

posts.title: Can I borrow a drill for one afternoon?

posts.author: Lena, Flat 22
posts.body: The tap in the bathroom has started dripping, just enough to keep me awake, and I have no idea which part has given up. If someone knows taps, I would be grateful for half an hour of help. I have a wrench and a willingness to hold the torch.

replies.author: Dennis, Flat 2
replies.body: That sounds like a washer. I can come by on Saturday morning and we will look at it together.

posts.title: My bathroom tap drips all night

posts.author: Omar, Flat 15
posts.body: I have an early train on Friday and the first bus leaves too late. If anyone is driving toward the station around seven, I would love a lift and I will happily share the fuel. One bag, no fuss, and I am good company before coffee.

replies.author: Aisha, Flat 17
replies.body: I drive past the station every weekday at half past seven. I will pick you up at the front door.

posts.title: Lift to the station on Friday morning?

posts.author: Edith, Flat 4
posts.body: I am eighty-one and I still like a walk on Sunday afternoons, but the pavements are slippery now and I would rather not go alone. If someone fancies a slow loop around the block at three, I would love the company. We can stop for tea afterwards.

replies.author: Sofia, Flat 29
replies.body: I would love to, Edith. Three o'clock at the front door, and I will bring the good biscuits.

replies.author: Mara, Flat 12
replies.body: Count me in too. The long way round past the park is lovely at this time of year.

posts.title: Anyone for a slow walk on Sunday?

posts.author: Sofia, Flat 29
posts.body: I bought curtains that are four inches too long for the bedroom window, and the tailor on the high street is booked for weeks. I have a needle, thread, and patience, just no idea where to start. An hour of your time would save me a month of tripping over the hems.
posts.title: Teach me to hem a pair of curtains?

posts.author: Dennis, Flat 2
posts.body: Forty years as an electrician, and I still keep the meter by the door. If a fuse keeps tripping or a socket has gone quiet, I will take a look and tell you honestly whether it is a five-minute job or a call to the professionals. No charge, but I never refuse a cup of tea.

replies.author: Alan, Flat 7
replies.body: Dennis sorted our hallway light in ten minutes last winter. The tea is worth it.

posts.title: Retired electrician — I can look at a fuse box

posts.author: Marcus, Flat 33
posts.body: I have a sturdy step ladder, a cordless drill, and a toolbox that has fixed half the flats in this building. Borrow any of it for a day or two, just knock on Flat 33 after five. Bring it back in one piece and we are even.
posts.title: Ladder, drill and toolbox to lend

posts.author: Aisha, Flat 17
posts.body: I drive to the station every weekday around eight, and there is usually one spare seat. If you need a lift, just say the word the night before. No need to share fuel, but good conversation before coffee is always welcome.
posts.title: Driving to the station weekdays at eight

posts.author: Edith, Flat 4
posts.body: I make a pot of tea and take it up to the roof terrace every Saturday at four, whatever the weather. If you would like company, come along — we sit, we talk, we watch the sky change. All ages welcome, and the kettle is always on.

replies.author: Omar, Flat 15
replies.body: Best hour of my week. Edith's tea and the view over the rooftops cannot be beaten.

posts.title: Tea on the roof terrace, Saturdays at four

posts.author: Jonas, Flat 41
posts.body: I keep four bikes running in this building and I am happy to teach anyone the basics: punctures, brakes, and squeaky chains. Bring your bike to the basement on a Sunday morning and we will fix it together. Tools provided, patience included.
posts.title: I can teach basic bike repair

posts.author: Ines, Flat 31
posts.body: I just finished a novel set in one apartment building, where forty strangers slowly become neighbours through a broken lift and a shared roof garden. It reads like this board feels. If you have ever wondered who lives two floors up, start here.

replies.author: Rosa, Flat 19
replies.body: I read it last year. The chapter about the parcel room made me laugh out loud.

posts.title: A novel about a building full of strangers

posts.author: Priya, Flat 26
posts.body: This cookbook taught me that a good supper needs one pot, forty minutes, and no apologies. The lentil stew on page forty is now a weekly meal in Flat 26, and the margins are full of notes from whoever borrowed it before me. Start there and ignore the fancy books.
posts.title: The best cookbook for one-pot suppers

posts.author: Jonas, Flat 41
posts.body: A short podcast series about the people who kept old cities running: the lamplighters, the lift engineers, the caretakers. Each episode is twenty minutes, perfect for the stairs while the lift is out. It made me look at this building differently.
posts.title: A podcast about how cities used to work

posts.author: Edith, Flat 4
posts.body: There is a slim book of poems about stairs, waiting, and small kindnesses, and it is exactly the right size for a pocket. I read three poems standing by the lift and nearly missed my stop. Borrow it from Flat 4 if you like.
posts.title: Poems to read while the lift is fixed

posts.author: Marcus, Flat 33
posts.body: I am running a small repair session in the basement this Saturday from ten to twelve. Bring a wobbly chair, a loose handle, or anything with a screw missing, and we will fix it together. Tools provided, tea afterwards, no charge.

replies.author: Lena, Flat 22
replies.body: My kitchen chair has wobbled since spring. I will be there at ten with all its screws.

posts.title: Saturday: fix your wobbly chair in the basement

posts.author: Sofia, Flat 29
posts.body: The sewing circle meets every Thursday evening in Flat 29, and beginners are genuinely welcome. We have spare needles and a box of donated fabric, so you do not need to buy anything to start. Come even if you can only stay for half an hour.
posts.title: Sewing circle, Thursdays in Flat 29

posts.author: Priya, Flat 26
posts.body: My sourdough starter is strong enough to survive anything, and I have more of it than one flat can use. If you have a plant cutting to trade, I will swap you a jar of starter and the recipe that goes with it. Fair trade, and we both end up fed.

replies.author: Ines, Flat 31
replies.body: Deal. I have rosemary cuttings from the roof garden with your name on them.

posts.title: I will trade sourdough starter for plant cuttings

posts.author: Jonas, Flat 41
posts.body: I am teaching a twenty-minute tyre-changing session in the bike room on Sunday morning. Bring your bike and a spare tube if you have one, and I will bring the rest. You will leave knowing how to fix a flat, which is worth more than any gadget.
posts.title: Learn to change a bike tyre in twenty minutes

posts.author: Lena, Flat 22
posts.body: I left a black umbrella with a curved wooden handle on the bench by the front door after the rain. It was a gift, so I would really like it back. If you picked it up by mistake, no worries at all, just leave a note here.
posts.title: Lost: black umbrella with a wooden handle

posts.author: Alan, Flat 7
posts.body: I found a single key tied with a blue ribbon near the bins this morning. There is a small brass tag on it, but I will not describe it here so the right owner can claim it. Tell me what the tag says and it is yours.

replies.author: Tom, Flat 8
replies.body: That sounds like mine. I will come by tomorrow and tell you what the tag says.

posts.title: Found: a single key on a blue ribbon, by the bins

posts.author: Omar, Flat 15
posts.body: My little boy left his red scooter by the bike racks yesterday afternoon and it was gone by the evening. It has a scuffed left handle and a bell that barely rings. If anyone has seen it, please leave a note here — he has asked about it three times already.

replies.author: Marcus, Flat 33
replies.body: I saw a red scooter leaning by the back gate this morning. It might be his — worth a look.

posts.title: Lost: my son's red scooter

posts.author: Mara, Flat 12
posts.body: There is a grey cat asleep on the warm pipes in the bike room, and it looks very comfortable. It has no collar, so I do not know whose it is. If it is yours, come and collect it — and if it is nobody's, it may have just adopted us all.

replies.author: Edith, Flat 4
replies.body: That cat visits my windowsill every morning. I think it belongs to the whole building now.

posts.title: Found: a grey cat asleep in the bike room
